x: How many Nobel Prize laureates have an IAU-approved surface feature on Moon named after them? Satellite craters (e.g. "Bohr A") do not count separately. Count each person once. Use IAU names in force as of November 2026. List each laureate.
notes: Found 54 supported laureates, including shared eponyms and the separately named Sklodowska crater for Marie Curie. Country-partitioned Gazetteer-derived lists were useful, but the search was not exhaustive and the count is a lower bound rather than a completeness claim; satellite craters were not counted separately.

rows.reason: Edward Victor Appleton is the same person as the already-listed Edward V. Appleton, the 1947 Nobel laureate in Physics commemorated by the IAU-approved lunar crater Appleton.

rows.name: Francis William Aston
rows.reason: Francis William Aston is the full name of the already-listed Francis W. Aston, the 1922 Nobel chemistry laureate commemorated by the IAU-approved lunar crater Aston.

rows.name: Patrick Blackett
rows.reason: Patrick Blackett is Patrick M.S. Blackett, the 1948 Nobel Physics laureate already listed. The IAU chronology includes the lunar crater Blackett.

rows.name: Henry Hallett Dale
rows.reason: Henry Hallett Dale is the already-listed Sir Henry Dale. The evidence confirms his 1936 Nobel Prize but does not establish an IAU-approved lunar surface feature named after him.

rows.name: Alexander Fleming
rows.reason: Alexander Fleming is the already-listed Sir Alexander Fleming, the Nobel laureate. The evidence identifies him as a joint namesake of the IAU-recognized lunar crater Fleming.

rows.name: Howard Florey
rows.reason: Howard Florey is the already-known Sir Howard Florey. The evidence identifies him as a 1945 Nobel laureate and the namesake of the IAU-approved lunar crater Florey (2009).

rows.name: Walter Norman Haworth
rows.reason: Walter Norman Haworth is the already-listed Norman Haworth, the 1937 Nobel chemistry laureate. The lunar crater Haworth is IAU-approved, adopted October 30, 2008.

rows.name: Cyril Hinshelwood
rows.reason: Cyril Hinshelwood is Sir Cyril Hinshelwood, the 1956 Nobel Prize in Chemistry laureate honored by the IAU-approved lunar crater Hinshelwood. He is already listed.

rows.name: Frédéric Joliot-Curie
rows.reason: Frédéric Joliot-Curie is the same person as Frédéric Joliot, the 1935 Nobel laureate in Chemistry. The evidence identifies him as the namesake of the IAU-approved lunar crater Joliot.

rows.name: Albert Abraham Michelson
rows.reason: Albert Abraham Michelson is the full name of the already-listed Albert A. Michelson, the 1907 Nobel Physics laureate honored by the IAU-approved lunar crater Michelson.

rows.name: William Ramsay
rows.reason: William Ramsay is the already-known Sir William Ramsay, Nobel laureate in Chemistry (1904). The evidence identifies him as the namesake of the IAU-approved lunar crater Ramsay (1970).

rows.name: John William Strutt, Lord Rayleigh
rows.reason: John William Strutt, 3rd Baron Rayleigh, is the already-listed Lord Rayleigh, winner of the 1904 Nobel Prize in Physics and namesake of the lunar crater Rayleigh.

rows.name: Charles Scott Sherrington
rows.reason: Charles Scott Sherrington is Sir Charles Sherrington, already listed. NobelPrize.org confirms his full name and 1932 Medicine prize; the lunar IAU names chronology lists Sherrington.
